title: Thermodynamic principles link in vitro transcription factor affinities to single-molecule chromatin states in cells.
authors: Schaepe, Julia M; Fries, Torbjorn; Doughty, Benjamin R; Ramalingam, Vivekanandan; Liu, Betty B; Crocker, Olivia J; Marinov, Georgi K; Hinks, Michaela M; Marklund, Emil; Greenleaf, William J
one_liner_zh: 该文结合体外TF结合亲和力测量与体内单分子染色质状态及深度学习模型，定量揭示KLF1的TF-DNA结合机制，核心聚焦TF-DNA互作且方法含AI建模，高度匹配课题。
abstract: The molecular details governing transcription factor (TF) binding and the formation of accessible chromatin are not yet quantitatively understood-including how sequence context modulates affinity, how TFs search DNA, the kinetics of TF occupancy, and how motif grammars coordinate binding. To resolve these questions for a human TF, erythroid Kruppel-like factor (eKLF/KLF1), we quantitatively compare, in high throughput, in vitro TF binding rates and affinities with in vivo single-molecule TF and nucleosome occupancies and in vivo-derived deep learning models. We find that 40-fold flanking sequence effects on affinity are consistent with distal flanks tuning TF search parameters and captured by a linear energy model. Motif recognition probability, rather than time in the bound state, drives affinity changes, and in vitro and in nuclei measurements exhibit consistent, minutes-long TF residence times. Finally, in vitro biophysical parameters predict in vivo sequence preferences and single-molecule chromatin states for unseen motif grammars.
abstract_zh: 调控转录因子（TF）结合及可及染色质形成的分子细节尚未被定量理解——包括序列背景如何调节亲和力、TF如何搜索DNA、TF占据的动力学，以及基序语法如何协调结合。为解答人类TF——红系Krüppel样因子（eKLF/KLF1）的这些疑问，我们通过高通量方式定量比较了体外TF结合速率和亲和力与体内单分子TF和核小体占据情况，以及基于体内数据的深度学习模型。我们发现，40倍的侧翼序列效应与亲和力一致，这归因于远端侧翼调节TF搜索参数，并由线性能量模型捕获。基序识别概率而非结合态时间驱动亲和力变化，且体外与核内测量结果一致，显示出持续数分钟的TF驻留时间。最后，体外生物物理参数可预测未见基序语法的体内序列偏好及单分子染色质状态。
